subject: Observability pricing — retention, tracing, and advanced dashboards
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: DataOps Team <dataops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability scope and high-level ask

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the intro last week — following up with a short summary of what ACME is trying to accomplish on observability for our LLM inference workloads. Our main asks: retention policy options for token-level traces, a tracing pipeline for latency spikes, and a lightweight advanced dashboard bundle for product analytics teams.

Attached is a short RFP with expected volumes and three sample workloads we’d like to instrument (batch embed-jobs, low-latency chat, and high-concurrency reranking). Can you share typical packaging/pricing approaches for these three concerns and any entry-level pilot pricing?

We’re on a relatively tight procurement timetable (Q1 decision). Procurement will need line-item pricing and any proposed credits or trial periods.

ACME RFP attached: ACME_RFP_v1.pdf (pdf)

—Ellen
Ellen Park
Director, Data Platform
ACME Health
ellen.park@acmehealth.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability scope and high-level ask

Hi Ellen — thanks, and appreciate the RFP. I took a first pass and sketched three packaging patterns that customers commonly use:

1) Essentials: 7-day retention for traces + basic dashboards. Best for low-cost pilots.
2) Production+: 30–90 day retention, sampled token traces, tracing alerts, and the advanced dashboard bundle.
3) Long-retain: 180+ day retention + full-token retention for legal/audit use-cases, with hourly export hooks.

I’ve attached a starter pricing workbook (redwood_obs_pricing_v1.xlsx) with per-token and retention multipliers plus a pilot credit row. A few questions to size the recommendation:
- Which of the three sample workloads accounts for most token volume? (chat vs embed vs rerank)
- Do you need full-token replay for auditing (Long-retain) or would sampled K/V traces suffice?
- Would ACME prefer a committed-usage discount or a seat/seatless hybrid?

I’ll loop in Kar (karthik_iyer) and Grace (grace_oconnor) from our pricing and product teams to propose a straight-line concession path we can present to procurement.

Attachments: redwood_obs_pricing_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Observability scope and high-level ask — pricing guidance request

Karthik, Grace — forwarding ACME’s RFP and my starter workbook. Key asks: retention tiers, tracing (sampled vs full-token), and a dashboard bundle. Procurement wants discrete line-items and a pilot-credit option.

Requirements and constraints from ACME:
- Three workloads (embed-heavy, chat low-latency, rerank spikes).
- Decision timeline: Q1.
- They explicitly asked for pilot pricing and a procurement-friendly term sheet.

Proposed approach: create three SKU bundles (Essentials / Production+ / Long-retain) with explicit per-token rates, retention multipliers, and a pilot credit (30–90 days). I’ve stubbed a simple cost model — see scenario_costs.csv attached. Can you suggest discount breakpoints for committed monthly tokens and any margin-preserving concessions for pilot? Also confirm what we can ship in a 30-day pilot for dashboards (hosted dashboards + limited retention).

Attachments: scenario_costs.csv (csv)

Thanks — Rafael
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability scope and high-level ask — pricing guidance request

Rafael — quick notes from pricing/product:

- Breakpoints: 1) up to 1B token/month (pilot/SMB), 2) 1–5B token/month (growth), 3) 5B+ token/month (enterprise). Suggested discounts: 0% / 12% / 22% off list for the Observability add-ons.
- Retention multipliers: 7d = 1x, 30d = 2.5x, 90d = 5x, 180d+ = 9x (applies to storage/trace processing component).
- Tracing: recommend sampled KV traces for chat; full-token only for regulated endpoints (Long-retain). Full-token retention requires a 30% surcharge due to replay costs and export retention SLA.
- Dashboards: advanced dashboards (custom panels + 30d history) can be part of Production+; Long-retain gets the dashboards + hourly export to S3. Pilot: offer a 60-day hosted dashboard window with 25% credit on the observability component, capped at $15k credit.

If we need to get legal involved for an exception to the 22% max discount, propose escalation to sales leadership and provide expected ARR uplift.

—Karthik
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: DataOps Team <dataops@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: Observability package options for ACME (pilot & tiers)

Hi Ellen — attached is a concise proposal with three package options (Essentials / Production+ / Long-retain), example line-item pricing, and a recommended 60-day pilot credit. High level:

- Essentials: 7d trace retention, basic dashboards, per-token processing $0.000015; pilot: 60 days, $6k credit.
- Production+: 30d retention (sampled token reads), advanced dashboards, tracing alerts; per-token processing $0.000012 after a 12% bundle discount; pilot: 60 days, $15k credit.
- Long-retain: 180d retention, full-token retention option, hourly exports, compliance SLA; per-token processing $0.000020 (includes 30% replay surcharge).

Attached: proposal_obs_packages.pdf and a term sheet draft (redwood_term_sheet.docx) for procurement. We can map to ACME’s RFP line-items for legal and procurement.

If you’d like, we can schedule a brief call this week to walk procurement through the line items and pilot mechanics.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposal_obs_packages.pdf (pdf), redwood_term_sheet.docx (docx)
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ACME Health Procurement <procure@acmehealth.com>, DataOps Team <dataops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Observability package options for ACME (pilot & tiers)

Rafael — thanks for the fast turnaround and clear options. Procurement had two quick asks:

1) Can you confirm a capped max liability for the pilot (we prefer a $25k cap) and add language about data return/deletion post-pilot?
2) For Production+ we’d like a stepped discount schedule tied to committed tokens over 12 months rather than a single breakpoint (0–1B: 0%, 1–3B: 10%, 3–6B: 18%, 6B+: 24%).

We’re happy to run the 60-day pilot if the cap and deletion language are in the term sheet. Procurement contact is Jorge Maldonado (jorge.maldonado@acmehealth.com) — he will handle the formal review. Can we get a redline-ready term sheet and a short call Friday to close pilot logistics?

—Ellen
Director, Data Platform, ACME Health
